title: Seattle's Jackson Street scene
summary: He spent time in Seattle playing all night on Jackson Street, learning from Julian Hanson, and was accepted by visiting musicians.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Would you go down to Seattle while you were living in Spokane to go...

Yeah, I went over to Seattle before. I was there for a year-and-a-half one time. I'd told my father... my stepfather that I was going over there to take a special course in pre-law. And I never went to one class. All I
did was go down to Jackson Street there, and play all night.
There was a Jazz scene in Seattle?

Yeah, it was very good, too. After hours. After hours always. Gene Coy's band was there. The bass player that was with his band is the guy that replaced Jimmy Blanton with Duke -- and I knew him very well. [JUNIOR RAGLIN] There were a lot of good musicians there. There was one piano player I learned a lot from up there. His name was Julian Hanson. And there was a tenor player who played like Lester Young, who I loved -- he was from Kansas City.
I loved...I liked Seattle. I always have liked Seattle. I like Seattle much better than Frisco. There's no music in Frisco. Not for me. Seattle got more goin' on than Frisco. Always has.
I've only been there once, but I liked it. You know, just for a few days. But it seemed like a friendly place.
Yeah. It's metropolitan, too. Of course, it isn't as metropolitan as Frisco, but it's pretty good.
So actually when you were a young kid interested in the music... When you would do things like meet Joe Thomas and so on, these guys accepted you and they were nice to you and all that?
Mmm-hmm. Especially when I played with them.
